title: Headache
hpi: {{patient_name}} presents with episodic severe headaches, palpitations, diaphoresis (classic triad), and paroxysmal hypertension. Pheochromocytoma is a catecholamine-secreting tumor of the adrenal medulla chromaffin cells. Rule of 10's: 10% bilateral, 10% extra-adrenal (paraganglioma), 10% malignant, 10% familial (MEN2, VHL, NF1). Diagnosis: plasma free metanephrines or 24h urine fractionated metanephrines and catecholamines (elevated). CT/MRI abdomen — adrenal mass. Pre-operative alpha-blockade (phenoxybenzamine or doxazosin) BEFORE beta-blockade (beta-blockade alone → unopposed alpha agonism → hypertensive crisis). Adequate alpha blockade for 10-14 days before surgery. Then add beta-blocker if tachycardia. Surgical resection (adrenalectomy) is curative.
